processing: Withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried in the gongfu black tea manner, from leaf grown in Jiangsu.
harvest_season: Not fixed for the name as a whole; as with other Chinese gongfu blacks, spring picking makes the finest grades.
appearance_dry: In Yixing's black teas, the best-known of the province, slender, fine, tight strands.
appearance_liquor: In Yixing's black teas, bright orange-red.
appearance_wet: As is typical of the class, soft reddish-brown leaf.
taste_profile: Yixing's black teas are described as fresh, mellow and sweet; other Jiangsu teas under this name are less well described.

brewing.notes: Ordinary gongfu black settings; slightly cooler water protects the finer, tippier lots.

vintage_note: Little is documented about how the name itself is sold. As usual for gongfu black teas, it would be current-year or recent-harvest tea, and in practice you are more likely to see a county name such as Yixing on the bag.
description:
Su Hong Gongfu simply means gongfu-style black tea from Jiangsu, 'Su' being the short name for the province. It is more a regional label than a single defined tea, and few documents treat it as its own appellation.

The nearest thing to a heart of the category is Yixing, better known for its teapots, whose black tea trades under the regional name Yixing Hong.

Method is the usual one for the class: withering, rolling, oxidation and drying. Yixing's black teas are described as fine and slender in the leaf, with a clear orange-red liquor and a fresh, sweet, mellow taste. For teas sold from elsewhere in Jiangsu, you will have to taste and see.

When buying, ask where in the province it was grown. A seller who can name the county and harvest is telling you more than the label does.
history: Little is documented about Su Hong as a named tea. Yixing, known in antiquity as Yangxian, was a tribute tea area in the Tang dynasty, but that was not black tea. Local accounts place the start of Yixing's black tea production in the Guangxu era of the late Qing, a claim worth treating with some care.
